extra.message: User-controlled 'expr' query parameter is passed directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is restricted, eval() can still be exploited for arbitrary code execution via method lookups on literals (e.g., "".__class__.__mro__ attacks).

User-controlled 'url' query parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(). An attacker can make the server send requests to internal hosts (e.g., 169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata, or internal services) or arbitrary external endpoints.

User-controlled 'packet_ref' query parameter is joined with BASE_EXPORT_DIR without sanitization. An attacker can use '../' sequences to read arbitrary files outside the export directory (e.g., /etc/passwd).

User-controlled 'name' form parameter is joined with BASE_EXPORT_DIR without sanitization and written to. An attacker can use '../' sequences to write arbitrary files outside the export directory, potentially overwriting system files or creating cron jobs.

User-controlled 'card' query parameter is rendered in a Jinja2 template with the |safe filter and returned as HTMLResponse. The |safe filter disables HTML escaping, allowing stored/reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) via arbitrary HTML/script injection.

User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to remote code execution by injecting Jinja2 template expressions (e.g., {{ ''.__class__.__mro__ }}).

lxml XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This enables XXE (XML External Entity) attacks, allowing an attacker to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via XML entity expansion.

User-controlled JSON payload is passed directly as a MongoDB filter query to find_one(). An attacker can inject MongoDB operators (e.g., $ne, $regex, $where, $gt) to bypass authentication logic, extract data through blind injection, or perform arbitrary queries.

User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse(). An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to arbitrary external domains (e.g., phishing sites) by providing a URL like https://evil.com as the lane parameter.

The request's Origin header is reflected in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any arbitrary website to make credentialed cross-origin requests, exposing session cookies and authenticated data to attackers.

The Authorization header (containing the bearer token) is logged in plaintext via logger.warning(). This exposes sensitive credentials in log files, which may be accessible to unauthorized personnel or leaked through log aggregation systems.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The session cookie is set with secure=False, meaning it will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. An attacker performing man-in-the-middle attacks can intercept the session cookie, leading to session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: A hardcoded default secret key 'local-dev-change-me' is used when the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If deployed without setting this variable, an attacker can forge arbitrary JWT tokens, impersonate any user, and gain full system access.

A hardcoded default database connection string containing credentials (dispatch:dispatch) is used when DATABASE_URL is not set. If deployed without configuring the environment variable, the hardcoded credentials grant access to the PostgreSQL database.

X-XSS-Protection is explicitly set to '0' (disabling the browser's XSS filter) and Content-Security-Policy is set to an empty string (disabling CSP). This disables critical browser security protections, making XSS attacks significantly easier to execute.

ssl._create_unverified_context() is used to make HTTPS requests, disabling certificate verification. This makes the request vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks, allowing attackers to intercept or modify the response.
